stories.headline: Domino's pizza night for Red Raiders Football
stories.summary:
Ordering pizza in Essex on Tuesday will help the Essex Red Raiders get to Kingston.

The Domino's on Arthur Avenue will give 20% of all sales from 10:30 a.m. to 11 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 24, to the football team. Essex won the SWOSSA AA championship and are going to the OFSAA Football Bowl Series for the first time in school history.

The money will cover busing, meals and other travel costs for the team's Nov. 27 game in Kingston. It will also help pay for a year-end banquet.

"These players have worked hard all season to make history," said franchisee Richard Falkner. "Now it's our turn as a community to rally behind them."

You can order at dominoswindsor.ca. If you can't order Tuesday, you can donate by Interac e-Transfer to stevekotyk@yahoo.com.

stories.headline: Esterbrooks Hat Trick powers Lancers
stories.summary:
Amber Esterbrooks scored three times, including a power-play goal, and Rebecca Noble stopped all 24 shots as the Windsor Lancers shut out the Brock Badgers 3-0 Friday night.

Esterbrooks opened the scoring at 9:23 of the first period, struck again at 17:46 on the power play and added an insurance marker at 10:11 of the third period, to complete the hat trick. 

Windsor outshot Brock 37-24 overall, including a 14-2 advantage in the second period.

The Lancers haven't lost in November while reeling off four straight wins helping them improve to 7-3-0 on the season, good for third in the OUA West. Windsor hosts Guelph Saturday afternoon at 4pm.
